title: K797v2: GARCH-MIDAS vs MLP -- QLIKE Bug Fixed

bug_fix.k797_qlike_bug: QLIKE formula used -log(s2)+r2/s2 (neg log-likelihood), always negative when forecasts diverge from actuals
bug_fix.k797_training_loss_bug: Training used -log(s2)+r2/s2 which is unbounded below (s2->inf minimizes it), causing MLP explosion to 1e38
bug_fix.fix_evaluation: Correct Patton (2011): QLIKE = a/f - log(a/f) - 1, always >= 0
bug_fix.fix_training: Correct QLIKE training loss = r2/s2 + log(s2) (bounded below, minimizer at s2=r2)

literature: Harvey et al. (1997) DM correction, JBES
conclusion: NULL RESULT: Neither GARCH-MIDAS (+1.18%, DM=-1.199, p=0.231) nor MLP (+0.07%, DM=-0.037, p=0.971) beats GJR at Harvey t>3.0 threshold. MLP and GJR are statistically indistinguishable (DM=-0.037). Consistent with K526, K784: ML/MIDAS adds no value over GJR for daily SPY volatility forecasting. This result is robust once the QLIKE formula bug is fixed.
limitations: tau uses EWMA not true Beta polynomial (Engle et al. 2013)
MLP hidden=16 -- limited capacity; larger models untested
log_s2 clamped to [-20,-2] to prevent overflow; may constrain MLP flexibility
r2 proxy for sigma2 is noisy (Hansen & Lunde 2005)
